publisher: CloudPirates GmbH & Co. KG (Artifact Hub verified publisher; same publisher as the nginx and rabbitmq picks)
license: Apache-2.0 (Chart.yaml artifacthub license annotation, read from the pulled chart)
caveats: The default image is Redis 8.x, which carries the post-7.4 tri-license (AGPLv3, RSALv2, SSPLv1; AGPLv3 is the open-source option) - the same engine-license consideration as any current Redis image. Raises the CloudPirates concentration to three components; the ranked alternates below remain the hedge. Surfaced by an Artifact Hub catalog sweep after the first survey pass; verified live twice (Artifact Hub metadata, then anonymous helm pulls reading Chart.yaml, the license annotation, and the values surface).

publisher: Valkey project (valkey-io GitHub org; Linux Foundation project). Repo active: pushed 2026-08-07, 24 chart releases in index.
license: BSD-3-Clause (repo LICENSE file; Chart.yaml carries no license field)
caveats: Engine swap, not just a chart swap: this deploys Valkey 9.x (RESP-compatible Linux Foundation fork), not Redis. Chart is pre-1.0 (0.11.0). No Sentinel mode and no cluster mode in the plain chart. Auth model is ACL-users, so there is no 1:1 mapping from Bitnami's auth.password/auth.existingSecret single-password shape.

publisher: OT-CONTAINER-KIT (Opstree Solutions). Operator repo active: pushed 2026-08-04, 1427 stars, 55 operator chart releases.
license: Apache-2.0 (OT-CONTAINER-KIT/redis-operator repo). Note: the helm-charts packaging repo itself has no root LICENSE file (GitHub license API returns 404).
caveats: Big catalog shape change: operator + CRDs + two-step install (operator first, then a CR chart per topology). Values live under CR-shaped maps, so no 1:1 Bitnami values mapping. Default image tag lags upstream (Redis v7.0.15; overridable). Keeps actual Redis engine, and covers standalone/replication/sentinel/cluster — the broadest topology coverage of the three.

publisher: Individual community maintainer (DandyDeveloper; descended from the retired helm/stable redis-ha chart). 170 releases in index; repo pushed 2026-06-15, 257 stars.
license: Apache-2.0 (repo LICENSE)
caveats: Fails the official-vendor/CNCF publisher bar: one community maintainer, no vendor backing. Default image is Redis 8.x from the Docker library mirror, which carries Redis's post-7.4 tri-license (AGPLv3/RSALv2/SSPLv1) — review image licensing for the catalog even though the chart itself is Apache-2.0. Sentinel topology only; no cluster mode. Release cadence is slower than the other two (latest push 2026-06-15). Separately verified negative result: no anonymous official Redis OSS chart exists — helm.redis.io (index HTTP 200) hosts only redis-enterprise-operator 8.2.0-13 (commercial Redis Enterprise, an operator shape), and anonymous Docker Hub token+API probes for redis/redis, redis/redis-helm, and dhi/redis-chart all returned HTTP 401.

license: Apache-2.0 (LICENSE file shipped in chart tgz; also declared in Chart.yaml annotation license: Apache-2.0)

Cosign-signed (.sig tags present in the registry; public key published via artifacthub.io/signKey). Publisher is a commercial consultancy, not the nginx vendor or CNCF; NGINX Inc/F5 itself publishes no plain web-server chart (verified: helm.nginx.com/stable index 200 lists only nginx-ingress, app-protect, service-mesh, NIM/NMS charts). The in-chart CHANGELOG.md carries a caution note but it only says the file itself moved to GitHub Releases, not that the chart is deprecated.

candidate: application (Stakater) — generic stateless chart running the upstream nginx image
publisher: Stakater (maintainer field in Chart.yaml: Stakater, hello@stakater.com; github.com/stakater/application)
license: MIT (no license field or LICENSE file in the chart tgz; measured from the repo LICENSE at raw.githubusercontent.com/stakater/application/master/LICENSE, HTTP 200, 'MIT License')

Still a plain chart (not an operator), classic anonymous HTTP repo. Company publisher with a long, very active release history, but not the nginx vendor and not CNCF. License is MIT rather than Apache-2.0 and is only stated in the GitHub repo, not inside the chart package.

candidate: app-template (bjw-s-labs) — generic stateless chart running the upstream nginx image
publisher: bjw-s (individual maintainer, me@bjw-s.dev, per Chart.yaml; org github.com/bjw-s-labs)
license: Apache-2.0 (LICENSE file shipped in the chart tgz; verified against repo LICENSE, HTTP 200; no license field in Chart.yaml)

OCI-only for v3+ ('index' status above is the measured anonymous ghcr v2 tags/list = 200; 'tgz' status is the manifest GET for 5.0.1 = 200; anonymous helm pull succeeded). Extremely widely used in GitOps home-lab/fleet setups and very actively released, but the publisher is a single individual, not a vendor or CNCF project, which is below the stated quality bar for publisher type; ranked accordingly.

Publisher is a single individual, not a vendor or foundation, so it clears the shape bar but not the preferred-publisher bar. Chart tgzs are GitHub release assets (redirect chain, final 200).
